newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rises on commercial,stop-loss dollar sales.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rises on commercial,stop-loss dollar sales.

text.p: The ringgit surged in Asian trading on Thursday, sparked by large commercial sales of the dollar/ringgit at 2.5150, dealers said.

"This triggered stop-loss selling below 2.5100," said a European bank dealer in Singapore. "Talk that Bank Negara has called for a meeting with CEOs of banks further prompted offshore players to unwind their dollar/ringgit positions."
Dealers said offshore players were speculating that the meeting would see Bank Negara introducing a two-tier market like in Thailand.
Banking sources said the central bank will be meeting the heads of selected banks on Friday to discuss routine foreign exchange activities of the banks.

"Bank Negara is calling a number of banks to talk about their activities and exposure in the forex market. This is quite routine," said a banking source. Market players said Bank Negara was unlikely to impose any capital controls.

"The market is expected to hold its breath given the intensity of the rumours, even though we still hold onto the belief that there is no need for such drastic measures such as restriction on swaps," said research house MMS International.
Dealers said talk of large buying orders by Japanese players and importers around 2.5100, however, curbed a further fall in the dollar.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5115/25 a dollar after hitting a high of 2.5020. It closed at 2.5148/53 in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
